newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Sterling sets its sights on 2.95 marks.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Sterling sets its sights on 2.95 marks.

text.p: Sterling's sights are firmly set on its old European exchange-rate mechanism central parity rate of 2.95 marks, and it only has to hold above 2.93 marks for optimism about its prospects to remain intact, analysts said.

The pound leapt more than five-and-a-half pfennigs Wednesday to 2.9430 marks, its best showing since May 1992. While it ceded more than a pfennig of its gains overnight, analysts see the setback as no more than a temporary phenomenon.
"In the short-term, sterling/mark yells for a correction, but 2.9450-2.9500 is realistic," said Ivo Pescia, customer adviser at Olsen & Associates in Zurich.

Sterling/mark was at 2.9375/85 at 0745 GMT from 2.9265/75 late Wednesday in Europe. Cable also rose yesterday, reaching $1.6785, its highest since January 17. It was last at $1.6749/59 from $1.6700/10 yesterday.

The pound has ratcheted almost 4.5 percent higher against the mark in the past two weeks, setting fresh highs on nine out of the 10 trading days. Some analysts questioned whether it could sustain this tempo for much longer.
"The market is trying to establish great things but it is a question of how much longer sterling can keep this pace up," said Brian Kiely, treasury technician at Royal Bank of Scotland.

"We are looking for a couple of confirmation days of its strength," Kiely said. Such a signal would come if sterling can hold above 2.9293 marks, a two-thirds retracement of its move down from the 1987 highs to the record lows in 1995, he said.
This would pave the way for a move up to 2.95 and above, according to the RBS analyst.
Sterling also has scope to make more headway against the dollar, but is seen using the $1.6720/30 area which proved strong resistance on the way up as a base on which to consolidate.
A pause in cable's rally which does not result in a break below this level will lay the foundations for a gains above $1.68 to the highs seen in early January, said Kiely at RBS.
